findings.evidence: Naming conventions, §Spelling: "Declaration names use American English spelling. So e.g. we use `factorization`, `Localization` and `FiberBundle` and not `factorisation`, ..." (documentation is exempt, declarations are not). Repo precedent is uniformly American: `IsFactorizationScaleIndependent` (EpsilonEridani/QFT/Factorization/Scales/Basic.lean:261), `IsLOFactorized` (QFT/Factorization/DIS/LO.lean:47), `RenormalizationConstants` (QFT/QCD/Renormalization.lean:34), `normalizedGeneratorDataOfYM` (QFT/PerturbationTheory/FeynmanDiagrams/YangMillsGaugeData.lean:172). This file is the only source of British-spelled declaration names in the repo.
findings.fix: Rename to American spelling throughout: `FactorizationHypothesis`, `factorizationHypothesis_def`, `IsNormalized`, `IsNormalizedSplit`, `isNormalizedSplit_iff_exists`, `exists_isNormalizedSplit_ne`, etc. Docstring prose may keep `normalised`/`factorisation`.

findings.evidence: Lines 111-118, 198-201 are all proved by `(Iff.rfl)`. Upstream precedent for an Iff that restates a definition: `theorem tendsto_def {f : α → β} ... : Tendsto f l₁ l₂ ↔ ...` (upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Order/Filter/Tendsto.lean:30); the rubric addendum lists `_def` as "restates a definition".
findings.fix: Name the three `Iff.rfl` unfoldings `isNormalizedSplit_def`, `factorizationHypothesis_def`, `isNormalized_def`, leaving `NuclearEffect.isNormalizedSplit_iff` as the only `_iff` of that base name.
findings.issue: `isNormalisedSplit_iff` (198) is a pure `Iff.rfl` restatement of the definition, while `NuclearEffect.isNormalisedSplit_iff` (205) is a different, substantive characterisation; the two share a base name in sibling namespaces under `Medium`, so the short name is ambiguous for a consumer opening both. Same misuse of `_iff` for a definitional unfold at 111 (`factorisationHypothesis_iff`) and 116 (`isNormalised_iff`).

summary: Every new declaration uses British spelling (`Factorisation`, `Normalised`), which the naming conventions explicitly forbid in declaration names and which contradicts the repo's own `Factorization`/`Normalized` names; additionally three `Iff.rfl` definition unfoldings are named `_iff` rather than `_def`, one of which collides with a substantively different `NuclearEffect.isNormalisedSplit_iff`.
